title: The Board's statement in Policy 2024-01 that Massachusetts pharmacies must keep naloxone in stock
rule_summary: Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2024-01: Naloxone Dispensing (adopted 1/11/24, revised 2/6/25) states that since all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, Massachusetts pharmacies are required to stock naloxone in accordance with M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C, and that pharmacies must maintain a continuous, sufficient supply of naloxone to meet the needs of the community. The Board's Retail Compliance Inspection Report sets out the same statement as an item checked at inspection (item 60) and cites 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) and (b) and Policy 2024-01. The Standing Order for Dispensing Naloxone Rescue Kits signed July 13, 2026 states that the Board of Registration in Pharmacy policy regarding the dispensing of naloxone under the standing order is available at the Policy 2024-01 address on mass.gov.
exam_relevance: Tests whether the candidate knows that the Board states that all areas of Massachusetts experience high incidences of opioid-related overdoses or deaths, so that Massachusetts pharmacies generally, and not only pharmacies in particular towns, are expected to keep a continuous, sufficient supply of naloxone, and that this is Board policy read with 247 CMR 9.06(2) and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C rather than a regulation of its own.

common_confusions: Assuming that a Massachusetts pharmacy in a town with comparatively few overdoses need not keep naloxone in stock.
Treating Policy 2024-01 as a regulation rather than as a Board policy statement that the Board's inspection report checks alongside 247 CMR 9.06(2)(a) and (b).
verification_notes: Read on 2026-09-16 in Board of Registration in Pharmacy Policy 2024-01: Naloxone Dispensing (mass.gov PDF, adopted 1/11/24, revised 2/6/25), in item 60 of the Board's Retail Compliance Inspection Report (mass.gov PDF) and in the Standing Order for Dispensing Naloxone Rescue Kits signed July 13, 2026 (mass.gov PDF), together with 247 CMR 9.06 (mass.gov PDF, pages dated 12/6/24) and M.G.L. c. 94C, s. 19C on malegislature.gov.
